faqs.question: What is the difference between analog and digital MEMS microphones?
faqs.answer: Analog MEMS microphones output an analog voltage signal proportional to sound pressure, requiring an external ADC for digital processing. Digital MEMS microphones include an integrated ADC and output digital audio data (typically PDM format), simplifying system design and reducing noise pickup. Digital microphones are preferred for modern digital systems, while analog microphones offer flexibility in analog signal chains. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for additional guidance and support.
faqs.decisionGuide: Choose digital for modern digital systems, analog for analog signal chains.
